title: GA-MSSR: Genetic Algorithm Maximizing Sharpe and Sterling Ratio Method for RoboTrading

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper proposes a Genetic Algorithm Maximizing Sharpe and Sterling Ratio (GA-MSSR) robotic trading strategy. It constructs 16 rule-based features derived from technical indicators using a grid search optimization over a training period. A genetic algorithm then optimizes the weights of these features to maximize a novel cost function combining Sharpe and Sterling ratios, generating positions between -1 and 1 without future price prediction.
extraction.universe: 6 major currency pairs (EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, USDJPY, USDCAD, USDCHF)

performance_metrics.context: 5-minute AUDUSD currency pair with 1:20 leverage
performance_metrics.evidence_quote: The best performing currency pair on the testing dataset is AUDUSD which obtained an annual return of 320% with a 1:20 leverage.

key_findings: The proposed GA-MSSR model consistently showed significant positive returns and outperformed benchmark models on risk factors like maximum drawdowns and return variance.
The GA-MSSR model achieved superior Sharpe ratios, maximum drawdowns, and average position metrics across all 6 major currency pairs compared to benchmarks.
The trading strategy does not perform directional price forecasting; instead, it utilizes optimized technical rule-based features to bypass short-term market noise.
Applying a 1:20 leverage to the GA-MSSR model yielded stable and consistent upward trends with minor drawdowns, achieving up to 320% annualized return for AUDUSD.
limitations: The trading system has not taken transaction fees into account due to different pricing policies by each broker and the time-variant nature of the spread cost.
